correctness.rationale: Exact no-tie rank identities, stationary two-sided rank-displacement ergodic theorem, geometric inversion tails and the classical occupation-count PGF give the almost-sure quadratic-rate Spearman constant. Independent sign discrepancies at each fixed lag and an ergodic long-lag bound yield linear-rate Kendall constant. Negative drift reduces by exact rank reversal. Proof gives all quantifiers and conditions; exact standalone finite tests verify key normalization but do not replace infinite proof.

value.rationale: Differentiates two standard concordance statistics under a natural, practically misleading phenomenon: independent nonstationary stochastic trends produce apparent perfect rank association at two different polynomial rates. Exact constants depend on negative partial-sum probabilities, enabling quantitative assessment of rank concordance in drifted time series. This is a structural classification, not a routine change of notation or one arbitrary numerical case.
